summary: Republican Sen. Thom Tillis did not run again, so the seat was open. Democrat Roy Cooper won, defeating Republican Michael Whatley.

candidates.name: Roy Cooper
candidates.bio: Roy Cooper is a Democrat and former governor and attorney general of North Carolina. He launched his Senate general election campaign in March 2026 with a pledge to make groceries and other costs cheaper.

positions.summary: Says he is running to make things cost less, starting with food and groceries, and says farmers are getting crushed by tariffs.
Says he would reinstate the expired ACA tax credits, reverse Medicaid cuts, expand Medicare drug price negotiation and cap out-of-pocket prescription costs.
Says he has a deep commitment to public education, having worked to raise teacher pay as a legislator and focused on public education as governor.
As governor, promoted federal climate grants and an executive order with a goal of conserving 1 million acres of natural lands.

candidates.name: Michael Whatley
candidates.bio: Michael Whatley is a Republican and former chair of the Republican National Committee and the North Carolina Republican Party. At his 2025 campaign launch he said, "We will fight for a strong economy, safe communities, an America that is respected around the world."

positions.summary: Says he supports President Trump securing the border and deporting criminal illegal immigrants.
Says America's economic strength depends on reliable, affordable energy and reining in Washington's spending.
Supports the 2025 federal budget law and its Medicaid changes.
Says education dollars should follow students so families can choose public, private, charter or home schooling, and backs the federal Education Freedom Tax Credit.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (political.org Nov 14 tally, AP called 34 of 35). Certified: the North Carolina State Board of Elections certified the results on Nov. 24, 2026 (board release). Shares are computed from the totals in the board canvass abstract dated Nov. 24.
